title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

reports.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

summary:
Angela Lipps, a 50-year-old Tennessee woman, was arrested at gunpoint in July 2025 and spent about six months in jail after Fargo, North Dakota police wrongly charged her with bank theft. She was held nearly four months without bail awaiting extradition, then about two more months in North Dakota. The charges were dropped after her lawyer showed bank records proving she was in Tennessee at the time of the fraud. She was released on Christmas Eve with no way home.

Lipps is now suing the city of Fargo and detective Lucas Heck for $10m. Her lawsuit says police relied on an AI facial recognition match from a fake ID and surveillance video, did not verify her identity or find probable cause, and lacked proper training on the technology. She says she lost her home, car, and belongings, and was denied medications and dentures while jailed. The city declined to comment on pending litigation. The suit seeks accountability and damages.
